items.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Nifty faces crucial 26,000–26,300 hurdle; eyes further consolidation
items.description: The Nifty declined 0.75% last week, facing resistance near 26,000. Analysts expect continued consolidation, with 26,000–26,300 emerging as a crucial resistance zone. A cautiously positive, stock-specific approach is advised. IT, banking and financial services remain sector leaders, while metals, energy and midcaps continue to lag broader markets.

items.title: Jaiprakash Power Ventures, CarTrade Tech among 11 smallcap stocks that plunged the most in a year, but mutual funds raised stakes
items.description: Over the four quarters leading up to September 2026, mutual funds steadily increased their holdings in about 16 Nifty Smallcap 250 companies, all of which had a market capitalisation of over Rs 15,000 crore. Of these, 11 stocks witnessed some of the sharpest share price declines over the past year, even as mutual funds continued to raise their allocation to these companies. Here is a detailed breakdown, according to data by ACE Equity.

items.title: Sebi working on new exchange for pre-IPO shares, consultation paper out soon: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
items.description: Sebi is considering a separate trading platform for pre-IPO shares, with a consultation paper expected soon. The proposed exchange will focus on firms preparing for public listings, incorporating investor safeguards and disclosure requirements. The regulator is also reviewing grey market practices and simplifying foreign investor onboarding to deepen India's capital markets.

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: 9 stocks that gain for 5 days in a row
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending November 27, the Sensex declined 1.17%, or 989.33 points, to close at 83,339, marking gains in three of the five sessions. Around 9 stocks from the BSE 500 index advanced in all five consecutive sessions from November 19 to 27, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 5% to 17%. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: LIC portfolio stocks! 10 stocks where LIC had the highest stake in Q2. How many do you own?
items.description: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) holds significant stakes in several companies across different sectors of the Indian stock market. Data for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, highlights the 10 companies in which the insurer had its highest shareholding, along with their respective market capitalisations and LIC's ownership percentages. Here’s the full list.

items.title: F&O Talk: 25,350 remains crucial support for Nifty, says Sudeep Shah; gives RIL, HDFC Bank, IT stocks strategy
items.description: Indian markets ended lower, snapping a two-week winning streak amid selling pressure across key sectors. SBI Securities’ Sudeep Shah discusses Nifty and Bank Nifty levels, IT stock opportunities, bullish outlooks on HDFC Bank and Reliance Industries, FII positioning, and five stocks showing promising technical signals for next week.

items.title: Smallcap investors are buying more than they can afford; the MTF risk few are talking about
items.description: Smallcap stocks account for over half of India's Rs 1.5 lakh crore margin trading facility (MTF) market, raising concerns about forced selling during market corrections. A Motilal Oswal report flags rising leverage, low liquidity and possible SEBI curbs as key risks for investors, brokers and the broader cash market.

items.title: Microcap winners: Greaves Cotton, Thomas Cook among 10 stocks with gains of up to 50%
items.description: Greaves Cotton, Thomas Cook (India) and Tanla Platforms are among 10 stocks that have outperformed the Nifty Microcap 250, gaining up to 50.21% over the past two months even as the index declined around 8% from its September 23 peak, according to ACE Equity data.

items.title: FPIs can trade in physically settled non-agri commodity derivatives
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has made significant adjustments to its regulations, allowing foreign portfolio investors to conduct trades in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives for the first time. Previously, such investors were limited to cash-settled derivatives. This strategic shift is designed to boost institutional engagement and enhance market liquidity, promoting increased trading activities and stronger market dynamics in the future.

items.title: FPIs buy some more, but D-St slips 1% on tech, consumer drag
items.description: India's equity markets slid over 1% on Friday, halting a four-week rally. The downturn was largely influenced by investor sell-offs in response to climbing crude oil prices and uncertainty on the global stage. Despite earlier gains in November, both Sensex and Nifty faced significant declines. While foreign portfolio investors remained active, domestic institutions pulled back. Market fluctuations are anticipated as global dynamics evolve.
